abstract: Manufactures usually adopt variable sales policies to deal with variable retailers. For perishable products, retailers make inventory management strategic to optimize their revenue. In this article, the problem of product buy-back in the supply chain is considered with demand uncertainty. We also provide what is the best time to take buy-back.

articleTitle: Thoughts and status quo on technological opportunity
abstract: Recent years, the importance of technological opportunity on technology innovation and technology selection is better understood by the researchers internal and abroad. Research has been done on the conception, the way to recognize and capture and realize technological opportunity, studies on which are broader. To review the status quo and tendency of technological opportunity makes it possible to explore and acquaint the nature of technological opportunity. Based on the drawbacks of the research done by now, we should realize that the process of exploring technological opportunity is a dynamic system, the main force of which is enterprises. And that is the center point of the whole study. Many other factors are as important, for instant, market demands, knowledge spillover, absorptive capacity, innovation efforts, social and even political factors, etc. A wise way is synthesizing as many factors to model the dynamic process of exploring technological opportunity.

articleTitle: Optimal retailer's replenishment decisions for EPQ model under up-stream and down-stream trade credit financing
abstract: The traditional economic order quantity models usually assume that the purchasing cost must be paid for the items as soon as the items are received. However, in practice trade credit is one of the main measures to promote the sale of goods. On the other hand, the retailer would offer the trade credit period to his/her customers. That is a two-level trade credit. In this paper, we develop an EPQ model for deteriorating items under two-level trade credit, where the demand rate of the items is dependent on the current stock level, and the inventory system with inventory-level-dependent demand rate is further extended. Then we provide the necessary and sufficient conditions of the existence and uniqueness of the optimal solutions that could make the average cost per unit time to a minimum. Easy solution methods are shown to find the optimal replenishment policy of the considered problem and some theoretical evidences are provided for retailers to make the practical inventory decision. At last, numerical examples are presented to illustrate the developed model.

articleTitle: Modeling emergency event and emergency response decision based on event evolvement
abstract: For an emergency event under uncertainty environment, in order to make a better decision, a new definition about emergency event is given, which is a set that the element is event attributes including key attribute, secondary attribute, environment attribute and disserve evaluation attribute, etc. And the response decision for the emergency event also is defined newly by a set including the decision of extracting attributes, determining decision object and choosing action. Then, for a simple barrier lake event, we model the response decision problem into a infinite period stochastic dynamic programming problem when the event is random and dynamic. And a numerical example is given, the results show that the model can solve the problem effectively when the state of emergency event and the action set are finite.

articleTitle: PWYW as a participative pricing mechanism in online service
abstract: As a new participative pricing mechanism, pay what you want (PWYW) has some innovative characteristics making it can be served as a promotional tool to attract customers, as well as a profitable pricing mechanism, though it gives the entire price control to customers. Because of many unique characteristics, it is difficult for online service providers to determine the price of their services. In this paper, we insist that PWYW can be applied to online services. Firstly, we analyses the classification of participative pricing mechanism, and the profitability of pay what you want pricing strategy. We then discuss why PWYW can be applied to online services and how to maximize this pricing strategy.

articleTitle: Research on move sequence between competitive supply chains under a common stochastic demand
abstract: Supply chain competition has demonstrated its popularity in the advanced business world. In such a sophisticated structure often characterized with uncertainty, the move sequence of each member may play a decisive role. However, this problem has been under researched. To fill this gap, this paper considers a competitive supply chain structure consisting of two manufacturers and two retailers, with one manufacturer and one retailer composing a supply chain. One supply chain moves first, and then followed by the other one. In each supply chain, the manufacturer is the leader and the retailer is the follower. We explore the effects of move sequence and channel power on the system performance under a common stochastic demand. It is shown that the first-move supply chain can make more benefits than its competitor in launching a new product when the relative power of the manufacturers in each supply chain satisfies a certain condition. Furthermore, we discuss the results and propose some managerial insights.

articleTitle: Forecasting model for logistics demand scale in Guangdong Province based on Grey System Theory
abstract: In this paper, firstly logistics demand is introduced and indicator items are discussed. Then forecasting of logistics demand scale is illustrated. And GM(1,1) model is discussed in detail. Based on freight traffic and freight ton-kilometers, a novel forecasting model using Grey System Theory for logistics demand scale in Guangdong Province is proposed. Experiment result shows that relative error of freight traffic forcasting for 2009 is 0.8576% and that of freight ton-kilometers is 0.526%. So this model is efficient for forecasting of logistics demand in local area.

articleTitle: Consumer decision process based on search engine marketing
abstract: As an indispensable part of network marketing, search engine marketing is influencing the production and business activities of enterprises. This paper will review the perceived risk, search engine marketing and consumer decision behavior and then discuss about their influence respectively. Information search behavior is not only a crucial part of consumer decision process, but the key factor influencing consumer decision. Based on the analysis, the results of this study is trying to fill these gaps of search engine marketing in academic research and helping managers make informed business decisions.

articleTitle: Retailer's optimal ordering policy under two-part trade credit financing
abstract: The main purpose of this paper is to investigate the retailer's ordering policy under trade credit offered by the supplier. The trade credit policy discussed in this paper is a two-part strategy, l.e. Finally, numerical examples are given to illustrate the theorems and obtain a lot of managerial phenomena.

articleTitle: Shortest paths subject to time-varying stochastic transit times
abstract: We consider a stochastic, time-varying shortest path problem, where the transit time on an arc is a random variable taking discrete values, and the transit cost on an arc is a known function of the amount of the transit time. Waiting at a vertex is allowed, at a waiting cost. By utilizing the discrete nature of the transit times and their probabilistic distributions, we develop an efficient dynamic programming algorithm to determine the shortest (cheapest) path from a source vertex to a sink vertex.

articleTitle: Empirical study on the correlation between moderate government expenditure scale and inclusive growth
abstract: This article mainly applied empirical and contrast research methods to explore the relationship between the moderate government expenditure scale and inclusive growth. And there is significant correlation between the two things in the Nordic countries(Denmark, Finland, Norway and Sweden (hereinafter referred to as the Nordic countries). That is to say, moderate government expenditure scale is the foundation of inclusive growth. The ratio of government expenditure to GDP is taken as the research object, and 1990~2008 years' data as sample, then the relationship between moderate government expenditure scale and inclusive growth is analyzed. And then, some policies and proposes are put forward. Simulation results indicate that there are no significant correlations between the ratio of government expenditure to GDP and gini coefficient, per capita disposable income of urban residents, the number of full-time teachers per 10000 population, the number of health technical personnel per 10000 population, the number of population attend primary endowment insurance per 10000 population, urban residents engel's coefficient.

articleTitle: Product demand modeling based on use cases in service marketing
abstract: In this paper a new demand modeling method for new products - product demand modeling method based on use cases is put forward. Compared with the existing demand modeling method, it has the following characteristics: first, from the perspective of new product development, meanwhile supporting variant design of existing products. Second, the detailed product demand information is acquired using the use cases in software engineering. Third, with motor products, the applied research has been made further. In this paper quality function deployment and use cases are combined to analyze the acquiring of demand information, then to define product demand fuzzily, finally to realize the mapping from the customer demands to product engineering properties. With the analysis a theoretical guidance can be provided for the enterprises to improve product design quality and to shorten new product time-to-market.

articleTitle: Benefit game and regulatory system of water pollutant emission trading
abstract: The key to support the emission trading in China is to establish an effective regulatory system. This paper sets up an incomplete information dynamic game model between government and pollution enterprise from the perspective of related subjects' interests. Through the equilibrium analysis, a conclusion is reached that if central government increases the punishment force to the local protection and public participate level, it can effectively restrict local government shield enterprise's violations. On that base, an incentive compatible water environmental regulatory system is established which both government and public take part in, to ensure the smooth implementation of emission trading policy in China.

articleTitle: Knowledge management practices and firm capabilities development: The moderating role of knowledge expropriation hazard in supply chain
abstract: Previous studies have established the significant relationships between knowledge management practices (KMPs) and firm capabilities development (FCD). These relationships, however, could possibly be moderated by knowledge expropriation hazard (KEH) arising from the opportunism of human beings. Based on knowledge management and strategic alliance research, the main objective of this paper is to empirically examine this moderating effect in a supply chain context. The results revealed that KEH significantly affected the relationship between mutual-codification practices (which is a component of KMPs) and FCD, but it did not moderate the relationship between high-interaction practices (which is another component of KMPs) and FCD.

articleTitle: A study on innovative evolution relationship based on ecological niche in supply chain cluster
abstract: The innovative evolution and development of supply chain cluster depend not only on the cluster competence itself but also on the participants' evolution behavior; the "ecostate" and "ecorole" of innovation of supply chain cluster determine different positions of firms in competition, cooperation and symbiosis, and reflect innovative coordination among members and influence of industry dynamic characteristics. Based on ecological niche Models, this paper reinterprets the "ecostate" and "ecorole" of innovation in a supply chain cluster under the ecostate-ecorole theory, and study the interaction mechanism of ecostate and ecorole in supply chain cluster from the supply chain cluster and environment. Finally, the coordination and innovative evolution mechanism are analyzed by using the diamond model.

articleTitle: Collaborative innovation and adaptive innovation process of network organization: A multi-case study
abstract: This paper intends to carry out study on collaborative innovation and adaptive innovation from the perspective of network theory and constructs the collaborative innovation and adaptive innovation model on the basis of the literature review of innovation, innovation process, the relationship between network and innovation, which means through special screening mechanisms, innovation products come forward on the condition of the interaction among the diverse heterogeneous network agents. Through the analysis and comparison among ten cases from four levels of individual, team, intra-organization and inter-organization, we verified the proposed innovation model to make contribution to innovation theory and network theory.

articleTitle: Customer voluntary performance: The effect of customer satisfaction and the mediating role of customer-company identification
abstract: Customer voluntary performance refers to helpful, discretionary customer behaviors that support a service company's service performance and quality. Drawing on identification theory, we offer an explanation as to why some satisfied customers display customer voluntary performance. Specifically, we hypothesize and test customer-company identification as a mediator of customer satisfaction on customer voluntary performance. The results reveal that customer-company identification partially mediated the relationship between customer satisfaction and two dimensions of customer voluntary performance, word of mouth and customer cooperation, but fully mediated the relationship between customer satisfaction and customer participation. It is concluded with a discussion of research findings and implications for both marketing theory and practice.

articleTitle: Experiments on education as a service
abstract: As student satisfaction surveys are a primary method of evaluating university faculty teaching performance, it is essential to develop an understanding of the factors driving course evaluation. Here we discuss experiments conducted to investigate the value of various service actions in the classroom environment. In particular, we focus on the offering of excitement needs such as giving candy, humor, in-class demonstrations, music and the like. The experiments were conducted on a class of undergraduate students in a university in Daejeon, South Korea. SERVQUAL, KANO models and Kruskal-Wallace (or Wilcoxan) tests are employed. We demonstrate that there are statistically significant relationships between the service offerings and the students' perception; this perception can influence overall course evaluation. Thus, incorporating factors that are more commonly associated with other classes of service such as restaurant service or entertainment service may improve the perception of service quality in education. In addition, we observe a known phenomenon that, to our knowledge, has not been measured in educational service. Specifically, we observe that there is a statistically significant spillover effect from one time frame to another when a service is removed. That is, the service is remembered in course evaluations for some time even after it is removed; there is a service memory.

articleTitle: E-learning support service based on interaction among local campus clouds
abstract: Some learners couldn't access the educational resources conveniently, though the number of educational resources in universities has been growing explosively during the past few years. In this case, learning support services in e-learning system are invaluable for distance learners with provision learning service support, however, the current e-learning system couldn't solve e-learning resource sharing system of interoperability, and can not provide appropriate learning service support for learners. In this paper, we propose a campus cloud framework for e-learning, the novel approach ensures that the quality and success of distance education are maintained, and the e-learning system based on Campus Cloud framework can play an important role in the development of distance education teaching practices with a growth in the utilization rate of those learning resources in university. It is, in particular, important for learners to get learning service support from e-learning based on cloud service in campus cloud.

articleTitle: The determinants of adolescents' behavioral intentions towards online services: Empirical evidence from online game industry
abstract: This research proposes a conceptual model with perceived value, satisfaction, subjective norm and individual characteristics (i.e., self-esteem, self-efficacy and extraversion) as key predictors of adolescents' intention to play online games. Perceived value is determined by positive factor of perceived benefits and negative factor of perceived risks. A survey was conducted to test the model. Most hypotheses were supported. Moreover, sub-dimensions of perceived benefits (i.e., ability expansion, playfulness and pleasure of control, telepresence and group identification) and perceived risks (i.e., psychosocial, financial, physical, performance and time risks) salient for adolescent online gamers were identified. The effect of perceived value on playing intention is mediated by satisfaction.

articleTitle: Multi-period vehicle routing problem with recurring dynamic time windows
abstract: This paper discusses a new practical variant of the vehicle routing problem with time windows (VRPTW), which originated from the regional transportation planning for oil products at a China National Petroleum Corporation (CNPC) branch in a northwest province of mainland China. Tanker trucks are scheduled to serve each oil station in multiple periods according to a recurring and dynamic time window setting. Refilling at an oil depot is always required after visiting an oil station, so it is safe to assume that the vehicles are uncapacitated. The problem is formulated into a mixed-integer programming model and shown to be NP-Hard. We found that the mixed-integer programming model is only solvable for very small impractical cases using exact methods, e.g., branch and cut, which is employed by the state-of-the-art commercial solver ILOG CPLEX. Moreover, due to the floating time windows imposed on the nodes, traditional local search-based heuristics with node interchange operators are not applicable. Thus, we adapt and propose an iterative time window partitioning heuristic that discretizes time windows into multiple time points with dynamic partition widths. Experiments show good quality solutions can be achieved for problem cases with practical sizes.

articleTitle: Sustainable development: A quest for logistics social responsibility among Chinese manufacturing firms
abstract: With globalization, especially after China's entry into the WTO, an increasing number of Chinese firms have experienced social responsibility barriers such that they lose international orders due to failure in meeting the requirements of environment, human rights or safety standard. This study attempts to shed some light on the mechanism underlying logistics social responsibility (LSR) in China. In particular, based on the five-dimensional structure of LSR framework, we propose that clan culture, business ethics, pressures from customers, suppliers, competitors, and law/regulations are important antecedents of five dimensions of LSR. A largely scale survey was conducted in China and a total of 162 firm-level questionnaires were returned. The results from a pilot study were reported. The contributions and implications of these findings are discussed further.

articleTitle: New service development in Chinese City Commercial Banks: A case study
abstract: After more than ten years' development, City Commercial Banks have made great progress, but at present the homogenization of banking products, restricts the development of the bank. Therefore, banks need to vigorously carry out the new services development. This paper, based on the literature review, taking a representative of Bank of Hangzhou as an example, through case study method, studies the process, organization of NSD and the barriers to it. The results complement the existing literature and proposed future research Direction, to promote the development of our understanding of the NSD in banks and the development of banks.

articleTitle: A survey of agri-food e-markets of China: A functional evolution perspective
abstract: How to build efficient e-markets for agricultural products has been a concern of China. This paper is to explore the agri-food e-markets of China from the aspect of evolutional functions, so as to shed light on the sound development of e-markets. A functional matrix is built based on the literature review of e-markets, and a survey of Chinese agri-food e-markets is conducted. It is concluded that agri-food e-markets of China show a binary scheme, with ordinary e-markets still in a preliminary stage, and bulk e-markets being in a priority to provide most functions. Future development of the ordinary e-markets should focus on providing solutions for settlement and after-sales phases. Bulk e-markets need to make efforts in providing collaborative process management.

articleTitle: The impact of service innovation on business performance: Evidence from firm-level data in Chinese tourism sector
abstract: This study examines the impact of service innovation on business performance in service firms in China. Based on RBV and innovation theories, we construct an integrative model which links service innovation, service quality and business performance together. 277 valid samples were gathered through survey questionnaire in China's tourism sector and structural equation modeling (SEM) approach was employed. The findings are as follows. First, service innovation would affect firm performance through direct and indirect paths in which service quality plays a positive mediating role. Second, the direct impact of innovation on performance is larger than that of indirect one. Third, the innovation mode adopted by China's tourism firms is a type of cost-reduction one which focuses on eliminating firms' internal cost of operation. Our findings provide a number of valuable insights for managers.

articleTitle: Exploring evidence-based medicine acceptance process based on a perspective of customer experience management
abstract: This study aims to explore evidence-based medicine (EBM) acceptance process of physicians. The perspective of customer experience management is applied to this study. A total of 32 in-depth interviews were conducted with 23 key informants and analyzed using the techniques of grounded theory. The result shows the acceptance process consisting of six stages: 1) perceived instrumental advantage; 2) perceived emotional advantage; 3) perceived anxiety; 4) communication improvement; 5) behavior influence; 6) omnipotent myth. This study provides an effective management strategy for hospital managers to diffuse an EBM system.

articleTitle: Macro-stress testing of credit risk for Chinese Banking sector: Two comparative approaches
abstract: With Basel II officially implemented in China, Macro-stress test exercises of credit risk are getting more and more important. In order to study the effectiveness of current methods in analyzing credit risk for Chinese Banking sector, Wilson model and quantile regression are applied in this paper. We find that QR approach can provide more refined results. Our Stress-testing exercises at the one-quarter horizon indicate that interest rate shock produces the most harmful effects followed by GDP growth and import growth, whereas distressed inflation and distressed housing price show little impact on non-performing loan rate(NPL), as an indicator of credit risk. Lastly, the simulated data shows that Wilson results tend to underestimate credit risk, which warns the practitioners that macro-stress testing generally employed may provide a biased direction.

articleTitle: The spillover effect of supportive leadership on brand image through employee brand building behavior
abstract: Through the organization management literature review, we know that the leadership style moulds the employee behaviors (Li & Wang, 2009). Due to the characteristics of service, such as intangibility and high personal interaction between customers and firm's employees during the service delivery process, the attitudes and behaviors of service people influence the customer perceptions. Therefore, the employee brand building behavior (EBBB), which is the bridge between the organization internal brand communications and customers perceived brand image. The study examines the spillover effect of supportive leadership on brand image through EBBB. We conducted a survey with over 1400 participants, consisted of 400 employees and over 1000 customers in 4 hotels in Guangzhou and Shenzhen, China. The authors used the HLM path analysis to test the effect of organizational climate of supportive leadership on the EBBB and test the cross-level effect of EBBB on the customers perceived brand image. The HLM results of data analysis reveal that (1) organizational supportive leadership has a significant effect on the EBBB; (2) organizational leadership climates have a spillover effect on customer level, such as the influence of organizational leadership flows to customers perceived brand image through the employee behaviors. This study enriches the theory about the spillover effect of organizational leadership on customer level. The findings contribute to help the service firm pay more attention to mould a supportive leadership climate to encourage the EBBB which will lead to a positive brand image.

articleTitle: Exploring the antecedents of technical exchanges and technology transfer in supply chains: A research-in-progress
abstract: Knowledge sharing has been recognized as a key enhancement of supply chain performance. However, the sharing of knowledge may not take place easily and automatically among the supply chain partners. This study attempts to shed some light on the mechanisms underlying knowledge sharing in supply chains. In particular, we focus on knowledge sharing in a dyadic buyer-supplier relationship. We posit that trust and power are two important antecedents of two types of knowledge sharing between a buyer and its supplier, namely technical exchanges and technology transfer. A large scale mail survey was conducted in Singapore to test our research model.

articleTitle: An empirical study of the impacts of supplier responsiveness on project performance
abstract: With the increasing amounts of research and practices of use innovation and quick responses to environmental changes, great attention has been paid to organizational customer innovation and organizational responsiveness as well. Based on supplier responsiveness to the organizational user innovation, this paper firstly explores not only the direct influence of supplier responsiveness on project performance, but also the indirect influence mediated by customer knowledge sharing, and then makes an empirical study in the context of China's telecommunication service industry. Finally, conclusions, implications, and limitations of the research are presented.

articleTitle: Games in the evolution of corporate social responsibility
abstract: This paper explores the evolution of corporate social responsibility by designing and analyzing games based on conditions close to the reality. Costs and benefits, which result in payoffs, are two most important determinants for rational firms' related decisions. In the gradual evolutionary process, external and internal factors, like the pressure from non-shareholding stakeholders and the profitability of slack resources, keep changing, interacting and thus significantly influencing the development of CSR. Though with some limitations resulted from the special analytical method, findings from the research points out new directions for further research.

articleTitle: Research on strategic service of third-party logistics
abstract: Based on organic organization, the nature of third-party logistics from the perspective of strategic service level is defined firstly in this paper. Then, taking service as the key factor and only advantage in competition, we propose the definition of "strategic service", analyze the nature of strategic service, clarify the difference between strategic service and service strategies, and build framework of strategic service for third-party logistics and construct strategic service mode of third-party logistics. This study finds that strategic service has strategic importance for third-party logistics, and our conclusions bring new management ideas to third-party logistics in dynamic environment and benefit the whole supply chain operation.

articleTitle: An integrated framework of tour guide interaction quality, tourist perceived risk and satisfaction
abstract: Tour guide service quality has always been the focus of controversy in the tourism service area. This paper constructs an integrated framework of tour guide interaction quality, tourist perceived risk and satisfaction, exploring the working mechanism between tour guide interaction quality and tourist perceptions. Using survey data from 517 tourists who have used tour guide service in China's four cities, the authors find that it is useful to lower the tourist perceived personal risk and enhance the tourist perceived value and satisfaction by improving the tour guide's attitude, behavior and expertise. However, the effects of interaction quality on non-personal risk and non-personal risk on perceived value and satisfaction are complex comparatively.

articleTitle: Is Chinese business education ready for services management? A survey into services management course development in Chinese business schools
abstract: As the focus of the Chinese economy changes from manufacturing to services, Chinese business education and research need to be refocused. In this paper, a questionnaire survey with 246 faculty members from 50 Chinese business schools was conducted to explore two aspects regarding services management (SM) course development: the status quo and the potential of SM course development. The survey shows that SM has been developing into a legitimate course in 48% of our sample business schools of Chinese key universities since 1990s; nevertheless, there are still quite a few constraints in SM course development. Based on the data results, some suggestions are made on SM course development. The implications of this report, its limitation and future research directions are also discussed.

articleTitle: Pricing decisions in a dual channels system with different power structures
abstract: This paper investigates the effect of product substitutability and relative channel power on pricing decisions under different power structure of a dual exclusive channel system where each manufacturer distributes its goods through a single exclusive retailer but two goods are substitute. A linear demand based on the utility function of a representative consumer is assumed, and three game scenarios on power structures are examined under symmetric and asymmetric related channel powers. It is shown that no power structure is always the best for the entire supply chain though all members on supply chain have incentive to lead the Stackelberg game. Meanwhile, the vertical Nash game is an equilibrium for the members, however, a Prisoner's dilemma necessarily incurs for the entire supply chain because the Retailer Stackelberg or the manufacturer Stackelberg can gain the better performance than that in vertical Nash for the entire supply chain when the product substitutability is moderate or higher and the asymmetric relative channel power is moderate, while consumers always get the most welfare from the vertical Nash game.

articleTitle: Price dispersion, information value and market efficiency in electronic markets: A comprehensive analytical framework
abstract: In this paper, we incorporate the proxies about price dispersion, information value and market efficiency in electronic markets into the same analytical framework for research, examine the explaining strength of existing literature on electronic markets form different perspectives. Based on that, we point out that price dispersion phenomena in electronic markets result from comprehensive effects of many factors. In the final, we outline the future directions for research, that is, in order to probe into the theories about price dispersion, measure of information and market efficiency in electronic markets, an comprehensive theory analytical framework that integrates those aspects influencing the price should be suggest through the introduction of price-comparison shopping diffusion model.

articleTitle: The impact mechanism of service quality on customer loyalty of individual investors in securities brokerage business — An empirical study based on SCSB model
abstract: The paper analyzes the influencing mechanism of individual investor's loyalty on China's securities industry by SEM. The result shows that customer satisfaction and service quality are the most important factor which affects customer loyalty. Customer satisfaction does not only affect customer loyalty directly, but also affects customer loyalty through complaint indirectly. The effect of customer expectations on customer loyalty is not obvious.

articleTitle: Scale development of customer value in China mobile service
abstract: Customer Value is widely discussed in the service literature. Little research has addressed the value construct itself in the Mobil service. This research describes the development of a 15-item measure, which can be used to assess customers' perceptions of the value at a service level. The measure was developed for use in the Mobil service purchase situation to determine what consumption values drive usage attitude and behavior. Three distinct, value dimensions were generated. They were termed service, brand and function value. The reliability and validity of the scale was assessed, using exploratory and confirmatory analyses. All three value dimensions were found to help significantly in explaining attitudes and behavior.

articleTitle: An empirical study on the innovation resource acquisition of service-oriented enterprise based on innovation network
abstract: In the dynamic environment, the service-oriented enterprises are becoming an important support force in social and economic development. The study on innovation resource acquisition of the enterprises is becoming one of the focuses in the theoretical circles and enterprises. In this paper, the relationship that between the linkage patterns of network and innovation resource is analyzed from the perspective of innovation network. And the theoretical model of the both is set up by using literature research method and qualitative research method. On the basis of this, and empirically tests the model with data from a survey of 330 service-oriented enterprises in 7 different regions in China. Results show that the model can serve as a means for enterprises to make a choice among different linkage patterns for obtaining effective innovation resource. At last, it put forward the future research directions.

articleTitle: Role of self-rationalization and perceived company web policy for employee personal web usage in the workplace
abstract: It is generally understood, organizations that provide web access to employees' in the workplace for work-related reasons, has the potential to be used for personal-related reasons. Personal Web Usage (PWU) behavior is a conscious decision making process for differentiating web-activity. In order to justify certain web-behavior, an employee will develop an attitude towards their own behavior which is a self-rationalization strategy. We propose this is a form of cognitive dissonance, similar to a `vice or virtue' decision. For employee web usage the two cognitions would be `work-related' or `non-work-related' internet activity. The present study extends to organizational literatures by conducting a usage assessment, examines attitudes for web usage during company time, and explores employee perceived company web-policy. An exploratory open-ended interview was conducted with a sample of 10 employees to analyze the employee attitudes for the use of internet technology at the workplace. The findings demonstrated distinctive employee web usage patterns where finding PWU to be not only permissible, but also rationalize its usage. We determine this rationalization and the PWU activity are directly conditioned or adjusted by perceived company web-policy, where strict or lenient perceived policy is seen as a threat or opportunity in levels. We conclude on the basis of our interview narrations of PWU experiences in having Individual, Process, and Organizational orientation. Our interview method and PWU coding can contribute to better profiling PWU for Chinese employees. These dimensions include separate categorical variables that we suggest can be useful predictors of the employee web-usage decision making process.

articleTitle: Review and prospect of the emergency resource coordination under unconventional emergencies
abstract: The coordination of emergency resources in the event of unconventional emergencies and large-scale disasters is of vital importance in emergency resource management. This paper discusses the main research content and the objective of resource coordination problem and to properly grasp the research trend, this study overviews and analyzes the research status of this field in detail through the identification of the resource coordination problem in literature that is mainly categorized into literature related to resource facility location problem, emergency resource allocation problem, and emergency resource scheduling problem. The formulation models are also summarized and the prospect for future research directions is finally addressed.

articleTitle: A transportation service procurement problem with combinatorial auction
abstract: This paper discusses a practical transportation service procurement problem, which is originated from an external project with the department of transportation purchasing at Royal Philips. A combinatorial auction strategy is developed to help the department to determine the annual transportation service procurement cost. Because of a few preset internal and external policies, to settle an optimal purchasing plan becomes a challenging job for the company. We formulate this problem into a linear integer programming model, and prove it is MV-Hard. We also find that the integer programming model is only solvable for very small cases with only a few lanes, bidders and bids using the state-of-the-art commercial solver ILOG CPLEX 11. We propose an iterative rounding heuristic algorithm that works on the linear-relaxation of the integer programming model. Experiments show that good-quality solutions are achieved for instances of moderate size.

articleTitle: A study of customers' bad behavior base on the psychological contract violation
abstract: Psychological contract has always been a hot topic in the researches of organizational behaviors. In recent years, scholars have started to introduce the concept of psychological contract into the context of marketing, reckoning that it exists not only in other fields of study but also marketing. This paper took catering services industry as our research object. Based on the review of literatures and questionnaire survey, we have verified in the structural equation model that the psychological contract between service enterprises and customers in marketing is constructed by transactional psychological contract and relational psychological contracts. On further discussion of the impact of service enterprises' psychological contract violation on customers' bad behavior., The results suggest that the influence of service enterprise psychological contract on customers' bad behavior entirely takes the customers' satisfaction as mediating variables. It offers new ways of thinking in reducing customers' bad behavior for service enterprises and it has significant practical and application value in the service enterprise customer relationship management.

articleTitle: Empirical research on factors determining China's OFDI location distribution
abstract: This paper uses 116 host countries' cross-sectional data to empirically analyze the factors determining China's Outward Foreign Direct Investment (OFDI) location distribution, and provides some recommendations on how to form the optimal investment policy. The empirical results obtained by WLS regression method show that host countries' market scale, economic risk, FDI policy, investment continuity, culture connection and technology level have significant effect on OFDI flow; while market potential, resource endowment, labor cost and political risk do not. The main contribution of this paper is the revelation of significant difference in the factors determining China's OFDI towards developed countries and developing countries by Chow test, which would further benefit improving investment policy.

articleTitle: A profit-maximizing supply network design model with vendor managed inventory
abstract: In this paper, we study a logistics network design problem with vendor managed inventory in which the company is in charge of managing inventory for its downstream warehouses and retailers, and can choose whether to satisfy each retailer's demand. The problem incorporates location, transportation, pricing, and warehouse-retailer echelon inventory replenishment decisions. Traditionally, these decisions are optimized separately. We formulate the problem as a set-packing model and solve it using branch-and-price. The pricing problem that arises from each iteration of the column generation procedure is an interesting nonlinear IP problem. We show the pricing problem can be solved in O(n<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> log n) time for each warehouse, where n is the number of retailers. The computational results shed insights on the benefits that the integrated approach can achieve significant cost savings. The computational results also highlight the efficiency of the solution algorithm.

articleTitle: Diffusion theory and behavior in industry concentration degree correlation: A case study of scenic spots
abstract: Local Industry plays an important role of regional economic development; the agglomeration degree of concentration reflects the ability of the index as a regional industrial development and prosperity and is closely related. Travel thriving and tourism economic prosperity is an inevitable outcome of a country or region which got to a certain stage of economic development. China's famous tourist attractions are so many which all over by various means and ways to attract tourists from home and abroad in different regions in recent years. How to evaluate these numerous kinds of favorable policies and economic effects of tourism has long been a weak link in tourism research. In this paper, we used the four major scenic areas in Jiangxi Province to analysis visitors spontaneous choice selection and infection choice selection with the theory of the proliferation behavior of, drew the conclusion that the scenic area management should be based on characteristics of its own tourist attractions, Anglicizing different types of travelers on the efforts, targeted the commencement of marketing and publicity, thus enhancing work performance, build brand service features.

articleTitle: The antecedence and consequence of customer satisfaction in higher education: A comprehensive model in China
abstract: Customer Satisfaction in higher education is regarded as a degree to which customers is satisfied with the education service in general. Literature review and empirical studies show that, First, service quality in higher education is a key prerequisite of customer satisfaction; Second, service price in higher education has no significant direct influence on customer satisfaction, but has little indirect influence on customer satisfaction in higher education; Third, service quality and price are determinants of service value, service value not only influences directly and positively upon customer satisfaction, but also influences indirectly and positively upon behavior intention. In the end, customer satisfaction is a cause of behavior intention in higher education.

articleTitle: An empirical study on the relationships among customer psychological empowerment, service fairness and customer attitude
abstract: Based on literature review, the authors proposed a conceptual model about the relationships among four service fairness (Distributive fairness, Procedural fairness, Interactional fairness, and Informational fairness), customer psychological empowerment and customer attitude including customer trust, customer satisfaction and customer citizenship behavior. We collected data from a bank in Guangzhou and explore the relationship among these variable using the LISREL. Results suggest that Distributive Fairness, Procedural Fairness, and Informational Fairness have significant effects on Customer Psychological Empowerment while Interactional Fairness does not. At the same time, results show that Customer Psychological Empowerment has direct effects on Customer Trust, Customer Satisfaction and Customer Citizenship Behavior. This study contributes to help the scholars who want to further empirical research on Customer Psychological Empowerment. It will also make great sense to those service companies who want to empower customers in order to improve their trust, satisfaction, and citizenship behavior.

articleTitle: The impact of business process modularity on relational contract in the outsourcing of two business processes
abstract: How to successfully govern the alliances of business process outsourcing (BPO) is worthy of research. This paper studies the impact of business process modularity on relational contract when two unverifiable business processes are outsourced, by modeling a repeated game. The results show that, enhancing business process modularity improves the sustainability of relational contract in BPO, and the client's payoff. When the relational contract is first best, business process modularity will not affect the optimal bonus which is a constant, and when the relational contract is second best, higher business process modularity is associated with a higher bonus.

articleTitle: How addiction behavior as a factor of switching barrier affects fans' loyalty in sponsoring professional sports games — A case study on the fans behavior toward Taiwan professional base ball games
abstract: The professional sports games as a unique form of service, provides people with differentiated benefits such as recreation, excitement, tense, and enjoyment with ovation. Although incidents in the dark side of sports games like cheating, gambling, even economics recession may impede fans' drive for continual patronage, "addiction" into participation in the sports games prevent them from quitting the events, if certain motivation factors like satisfaction, switching cost, and the adoration toward specific sports stars are isolated. This study makes an effort to explore a novel research topic in consumer behavior under the context of sports service, by investigating the role of addiction in switching barrier for sponsoring professional baseball game events. The outcome of this empirical research justifies addiction as one factor of switching barrier and also reveals a very interesting finding, namely, the effect of fans satisfaction on loyalty is relatively weak, while with the mediation of switching barrier, the link between satisfaction and loyalty are much more reinforced. Management of professional baseball team may formulate strategies based on this theoretical exploration. The finding will fill the gap of extant literature in sports service marketing, and make contribution to provide an insight into the behavior of sports fans to allow sports service providers to formulate appropriate strategies to enhance consumers' "stickiness" in professional sports game participation, so as to add the odds of business success.

articleTitle: A P2P Campus Grid framework for e-learning
abstract: The number of educational resources in universities has been growing explosively during the past few years, on the other hand, although e-learning system could provide learning service access for learners, some learners couldn't access the educational resources conveniently. At the same time, the current e-learning system couldn't solve e-learning resource sharing system of interoperability, and can't provide good quality of service for learners. In this paper, we propose a P2P Campus Grid framework based grid service for e-learning. The new framework has a growing interest in raise the utilization rate of learning resources in university, and, learners who want to learn from the e-learning system could ubiquitously access the learning service provided by a hybrid P2P Grid technology over campus networks.

articleTitle: The empirical research on interorganizational trust in firm network relationships — Factors, path and mechanism
abstract: Today, Firm networks are receiving an increasing attention in China. Interorganizational trust is the basis of formation and operation of the network organization. Previous studies are most focus on the trust in bureaucratic organizations, interorganizational trust among network partners has been little researched. The study explores the factors which influence interorganizational trust creation in firm networks, it also investigates how they work and the interrelationship of them. In the survey, 4 latent variables and 39 observed variables are conducted in structural equation model (SEM). It finds that network strategic security will significantly enhance the interorganizational trust among network partners and so on. Furthermore, the implications for alliance managers are also discussed.

articleTitle: Similarities and differences between product and service innovation: An empirical analysis of Jiangsu province's panel data
abstract: This paper aims to provide an initial step towards a synthesis of service and product research. Using a baseline model of innovation, applicable to innovation in general, we hypothesize differential context effects between service and product in order to better understand their differences and similarities. The results provide initial support for the integrating perspective.

articleTitle: Trade credit, traditional credit and monetary policy transmissions: Evidence from Chinese firms
abstract: This paper investigates the determinants and roles of trade credit (informal financing channel) and traditional credit (formal financing channel) based on a sample of 674 listed firms from the manufacturing sector in China during monetary policy transmissions over 2001-2007. Our evidence supports that trade credit likely plays a complementary role to traditional credit, and that the imperfect credit market view rather than the redistribution view accounts for the complementary hypothesis according to our sample.

articleTitle: Content, fulfilment and prospects of ideology-infused psychological contract
abstract: Literature on the ideology-infused psychological contract has arose over the last few years to be one of forefront issue in psychological contract domain. This paper addresses the central problems presently confronting the theoretical side of ideology-infused contract, including its content, fulfillment, and cause and consequence variables. In seeking to in-depth understanding and studying the ideology-infused contract, the authors finally point out four future directions on the basis of a more critical and comprehensive literature analysis.

articleTitle: Linear programming solution for transporting multiple petroleum products using pipelines
abstract: This paper describes a three-phase optimization model for the transportation of multiple petroleum products using pipelines, where the aim is to ensure that all depots are able to fulfill their demand for each petroleum product while minimizing costs. The first phase involves solving a mixed integer programming model for making resource allocation plans, which minimizes the number of products transported for each time period. The second phase uses the output from the first phase as the input to a quadratic mixed integer programming model to create a scheduling plan, which minimizes pumping costs by selecting the optimal pumping configuration and flow rate. We employ dynamic programming to increase the efficiency of the algorithm, which enables a commercial linear programming solver to solve problem instances of practical size. Finally, the third phase post-processes the solution from the second phase to minimize mixture cost using dynamic programming. This research was conducted on behalf of a prominent petroleum company in mainland China, resulting in annual savings exceeding 1 million Yuan.

articleTitle: Integrating fuel consumption and vessel emissions into berth allocation
abstract: This paper focuses on the berth allocation problem in the container terminal, considering fuel consumption and vessel emissions. By regarding the arrival times of vessels as decision variables and introducing the relationship between the fuel consumption rate and the sailing speed in the form of general power functions, we obtain a more elaborate model on the berth allocation, considering fuel consumption, than ever before. In order to overcome the computational complexity, we cast the original mixed integer nonlinear programming model as a mixed integer second order cone programming model. Furthermore, based on the fuel consumption calculation, we conduct the vessel emission calculation with the widely-used emission factors. Numerical experiments show that the proposed model can significantly reduce the fuel consumption and the vessel emissions in sailing periods, without lowering the service level of the terminal. This effort on maritime emissions is consistent with the environmental concerns of the international maritime organization.

articleTitle: Oil product transportation with combinatorial auctions
abstract: This paper discusses a new practical variant of the vehicle routing problem with time windows (VRPTW) that incorporates a combinatorial auction (CA) problem, which originated from the regional transportation planning of oil products for a prominent Chinese petroleum company. During peak seasons, the petroleum company needs to outsource some transportation projects to third party logistics (3PL) providers because the demand for oil products and the corresponding transportation requirements at this time are considerably higher. To minimize the total cost of oil product transportation from the depots to the oil stations, we integrate the CA and the VRPTW problems into a single problem, called the combinatorial auction and vehicle routing problem with time windows. The problem is formulated into a mixed-integer programming model and shown to be NP-hard. We devise a heuristic to separate all the stations into two types (whether to outsource to 3PL companies) according to distance. We then obtain an initial solution by separately solving the CA and VRPTW problems. To improve the initial solution, we design and test multiple heuristic operators to interactively solve the CA and VRPTW. Experiments show that good quality solutions are achieved for problem cases of practical scope.

Author Keywords: Vehicle routing problem with time windows

articleTitle: Is there research and development in services? A review
abstract: With the rapid development of the global economy, the world has entered the era of service economy today. However, the service research and development (R&D) activities remain a sporadic, occasional and non-system state. Long-term sustainability of this phenomenon will obviously undermine the economic vitality. First, we briefly introduced the status of research and development of services. Then, we comprehensively summarized the four areas of service R&D, including the concept of the service R&D, measurable indicators, impetus mechanism, and implement management. The literature confuse between the theory of manufacturing R&D and the practice of service R&D, and between the research and development. The conclusion is that, we should expand the concept of service R&D from the both sides of knowledge creation and knowledge application and acquirement, to establish the comprehensive framework of service R&D. Finally, we gave the future research directions.

articleTitle: Analysis of strategic supply management: A switching cost view
abstract: Strategic supply management, characterized by limited number of suppliers with long-term relationship and improved inter-firm communications, has become an important strategy for manufacturers nowadays. Studies on transaction cost analysis try to reduce supply chain costs, whereas those on resource dependence theory try to obtain and control more critical resources through strategic supply coordination and collaboration. In general, an extra cost will be incurred if a firm is switched out of the current supply chain network, which can also be defined as a switching cost. In this paper, we analyze the effectiveness of strategic supply chain from a switching cost perspective. We find that switching cost can be used as a yardstick to evaluate strategic supply management, with respect to strategic partnership and collaboration. The case of Ford Motor Company is used as an example to illustrate practical applications.

articleTitle: The empirical research of the influence of ERP's implementation on enterprise's internal control effect
abstract: This paper considers the influence of ERP's implementation on the enterprise internal control effect with the method of empirical, It is based on the data of the enterprises which implement ERP in 2008 as the research object, take internal control's three big goals as the starting points and are in view of ERP implementation process in correlation factor. The findings suggest that ERP's brand and number of years of implementation that can obviously promote enterprise's business efficiency are positive to the enterprise business efficiency. But the ERP's brand is negative to the effectiveness of operations. Meanwhile, the implementation age and the enterprise illegal activities are remarkable related. It means that with years of implementation increased, the artificial operation to the system data would possibly happen through the social familiarity with ERP system. In the end, it causes enterprise illegal behavior and unlawful act happen.

articleTitle: Evolutionary game analysis of emergency management cooperation for water disaster
abstract: Multi-stakeholders' cooperation is crucial to the emergency management for water disaster(WDEM). In order to discuss the cooperation problem, the paper mainly includes following aspects: (1) the network of heterogeneous agents about WDEM was built and game relationships among heterogeneous agents were analyzed; (2) the influence of behavioral strategies - cooperation or noncooperation - were observed and studied on reaching the cooperation of WDEM, and the evolutionary game(EG) theory was applied to analyze the cooperation of WDEM. Finally, the conclusion was obtained that to strengthen supervision of WDEM and to punish severely to noncooperation is very important to reach good cooperation orders.

articleTitle: How do Chinese listed companies adjust their capital structure toward targets?
abstract: Based on partial adjustment model, this paper suggests an empirical framework to examine the adjustment speed of capital structure with a specific adjustment approach, including commercial credit, short-term debt, long-term debt, stock and retained earnings. The main findings are followed. Most capital structure adjustments of Chinese listed companies occur by external finances. Issuing stock is the most effective adjustment approach, while retained earnings is with the slowest adjustment speed. The adjustment speed of external finances in financial surplus companies is higher than the one in financial deficit companies. Both financial situation and ownership nature affect the approach speed. Adjustment by issuing stock in non-state-owned companies is more effective than the one in state-owned companies.

articleTitle: The relationship-specific investment of suppliers / customers and capital structure: An empirical study based on industry-level data
abstract: Based on industrial-level dates of china, we investigate the link between corporate capital structure and the relationship-specific investments by its suppliers and customers. We find firms that deal with high intensity of R&D expenditure of suppliers and customers choose lower leverage. We also find the concentration levels in supplier and customer industries are positively related to the firm's leverage.

articleTitle: The impact of excess liquidity on the domestic food price inflation — Analysis based on the structural VAR
abstract: The different price elasticity of supply leads to the differences in a dynamic pattern of price adjustment to a global liquidity shock in the short run, but the products with low elasticity such as the agricultural commodity may cause an "overshooting" price in the short run. This paper attempts to confirm which has the more effect on our domestic food price inflation, U.S liquidity excess or China liquidity surplus. The U.S. excess liquidity has an impact on the domestic food price inflation through the transmission mechanism of the international commodity and the domestic excess liquidity. By means of the structural vector auto-regression model, the paper finds that the effect of imported excess liquidity and the commodity price on the food-driven inflation is less than that of the domestic liquidity surplus.

articleTitle: The optimal strategies in a two-echelon supply chain with risk-aversion and customers rebates
abstract: Consider a supply chain consisting of one risk-averse retailer and one risk-neutral manufacturer with endogenous manufacturer rebates (rebate to consumers), and the demand faced by the retailer is stochastic, price-dependent. We adopt Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) as the retailer's decision criterion. The demand uncertainty is assumed to be multiplicative, and the expected demand depends on the effective price of the product. We characterize the manufacturer and retailer's optimal strategies simultaneously. We show the existence of Nash equilibrium between the manufacturer and the risk-averse retailer.

articleTitle: Application service supply chain coordination with free trial
abstract: Free trial is a common used strategy in the marketing, which can promote the product or service adoption. In this paper, we examine the free trial strategy used in the service operation management. The free trial strategy is used to deal with uncertain market demand and stimulate the demand in an application service supply chain, which consists of an application service provider (ASP) and an application service infrastructure provider (AIP). We find the free trial can incentive the demand and minimize the risk of the application service supply chain caused by the uncertain market demand. Most importantly, a cost sharing strategy is proposed to make the decentralized supply chain achieve the centralized supply chain's performance. In addition, numerical example is analyzed to validate the proposed method and to provide more managerial insights.

articleTitle: Competitive analysis of gold trading and its risk-reward model
abstract: Gold trading is a typical online decision problem in our real life. Considering the actual situation, the investors may have some forecast for the trend of gold price. In order to receive better income they would rather take some risks. Considering the situation that gold price will exceed m in the future, we present the risk-reward model and give the new online pricing strategy. Then the competitive ratio is obtained. Finally, the numerical analysis shows the improvement of competitive ratio in the new prediction and the impact on constraint competitive ratio γ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">A</sub>' by the risk tolerance d and forecast m.

articleTitle: A framework for adaptive management system of water resources facing climate change — A case of Huai river basin
abstract: Climate change has produced an effect on the balance between supply and demand of water resources. From the view of new institutional economics, the paper introduces a conceptual framework for adaptive management system of river basin water resources facing climate change. It describes the interaction of the water environment and human activity under the situation of climate change through the PSR (pressure-stress-response) model, and seeks for the approach to multistakeholder seamless cooperation in order to achieve interest equilibrium and the sustainable development of nature, economy and society. At last, taking the Huai river basin as an example, a decision support system of adaptive management of water resources is set up.

articleTitle: Designing dynamic management based on customer-focused view
abstract: Based on customer-focused view this paper develops new constructs, explicit needs/demand concerning customers' willingness to pay (WTP) out of which Norm as Ideal comes out as a significant strategic guideline for explaining value creation universally at any time to any firm in any industry in all circumstances. And it dares design dynamic management to deal with innovation adapting to needs evolution for obtaining adaptive goodness with the standpoints of holism/synthesis/ dynamism.

articleTitle: Research on customer demand cluster method based on "graph"
abstract: Customer demand cluster analysis is an important basis of customer classification in management decision. With the development of structural models on customer's demands, the application of traditional cluster method based on demand characteristic vector is limited. In this paper, according to customer demand logic, we drew lessons from "Concept Graph" to define the formal structure of demand "graph". Based on this view, we proposed a model of Demand Structure Graph Cluster Pattern(DSG-CP), including: Similarity judgment and distance algorithm on different demand structural "graphs"; Clustering center selection of demand "graph"; Improved clustering algorithm and implementary system process. Finally, we verified the algorithm with customers' data of mobile communications in a certain region.

articleTitle: Quality constraint driven local optimization for efficient service composition
abstract: Service composition can aggregate atomic Web services developed independently by their providers. However, with the increasing number of candidate services, the solutions based on global optimization and constraints cost much computation time, which make them inappropriate for real-time applications. In this paper, a heuristic service composition method, named LOEM-T (Local Optimization and Enumeration Method with Solution Tendency Estimation), is proposed. It aims to keep a small number of promising candidates for each task in service composition. As stringent constraints may lead to no feasible solutions, a notion of stringent degree, that can describe the influence of global constraints, is proposed. Then with the help of stringent degree, the candidates that are more excellent in the stringent constraints are prone to be preserved. The results of experimental evaluation shows that our approach is feasible and can achieve a near-optimal solution very efficiently.

articleTitle: Stochastic comparisons in a price-dependent newsvendor problem with emergency procurement
abstract: We consider a newsvendor problem with price-dependent demand and emergency purchase option allowed after the realization of random demand. By stochastic comparisons, we investigate the effects of demand uncertainty on pricing and order quantity decisions as well as expected profit of the newsvendor, under second order stochastic dominance. Our findings include: (i) in general, a less variable demand shock leads to a higher expected profit for both additive and multiplicative demand models; (ii) a less variable demand shock has no effect on price for the additive demand model, while leads to a higher price for the multiplicative demand model. The implications of these findings for pricing and order quantity are discussed.

articleTitle: Bullwhip effect model and analysis of a supplementary product in supply chains
abstract: The story of "Walmart Nappies and Beer" inspires researches to find the potential relationship between a focal product (or item/SKU) and some other products (we call supplementary products here) in a supply chain. How to reflect the dependent demand relationship between a supplementary product and a focal product is significant for supply chain management and operations management. This paper investigates the bullwhip effect of a supplementary product in a two echelon (wholesale-supplier) serial supply chain. With the assumption of a first-order autoregressive demand process of the focal product and order-up-to (OUT) inventory policy, the analytical quantitative model of bullwhip effect for the supplementary product is established based on the simple moving average. The deduced model is further compared with the model without the effect of focal products. The obtained managerial insights is that in order to reduce the bullwhip effect of a product in a supply chain, exploring and sharing the demand information about dependent products is a feasible way besides information sharing on various echelons.

articleTitle: Competitive analysis of online procurement auctions for indivisible goods
abstract: This paper studies procurement auctions in an internet setting where the bidders, which are suppliers, arrive at different times and the auction mechanism (or the purchasing agent) is required to make decisions about each bid as it is received. We call this auction online procurement auction. Specifically, in this paper we discuss the discrete case caused by the finite divisible goods and assume that the demand curve of purchasing agent is one of indivisible goods, which is known. Finally, we present the discrete online procurement auctions strategy (called DOPA) for a certain amount of finitely divisible goods. Furthermore, the competitive analyses of DOPA are discussed and the competitive ratio is obtained.

articleTitle: Product quality improvement and free replace warranty sharing contracts
abstract: A contract mechanism to coordinate the supply chain's decision of product quality in conjunction with a free replacement warranty is proposed in this paper. Considering a supply chain with one manufacturer and one supplier, three schemes of contracts are examined, namely first best, no FRW cost sharing and with FRW cost sharing. Our conclusions show that FRW cost sharing contracts have the potential to improve coordination within a supply chain (even though full coordination is ruled out). The model built is a starting point for studying a wide range of contracts for procurement of spare parts, and for setting optimal length of warranty periods.

articleTitle: A study on spatio-temporal differences in operating efficiency of Chinese tourist hotels
abstract: Tourist hotels are the most important composing portion of Chinese tourism industry and its operating efficiency will impact the development of tourism industry. This paper analyses annual changing situation and regional difference in hotels' operating efficiency and its effect factors with factor analysis, cluster analysis and regression analysis based on panel data by nineteen financial indexes such as ROE and ROA, et al. The result indicates the operation efficiency of tourist hotels in eastern coastal area excels that in mid-western area; the stimulating factors of hotels' operation efficiency include the number of rooms, the average occupancy rate of guest rooms and integrative price of guest rooms, and its counteracting factors are the number of medium-priced rooms and residents' consumption capability.

articleTitle: Total economic capital modeling based on Copula function
abstract: In this paper we present a new approach to calculate the total economic capital required to protect a financial institution against possible losses. The approach takes into account credit, operational and market risk types and their correlation. It applies Copula to aggregate the total risk and in this respect improves upon the conventional practice that assumes perfectly correlated risks. A more rational way of thinking for economic capital calculation in financial institutions was then provided.

articleTitle: Empirical analysis of Zhejiang FDI and services development
abstract: Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) can promote the level of services development, which is important symbol of economic and social modernization. It has been making great contributions to the development of service industry during the past decades in China. This paper will use stability analysis, co-integration and Granger causality test to investigate the relationship between FDI and the development of Zhejiang's service industries, and give proposals on promoting the development of service industry.

articleTitle: To investigate the development process of the most popular blog through chaos theory
abstract: The study analyzes Wan Wan's Comic Blog by adopting "Chaos-Time" approach, and concludes that chaos situation exists in the blog development behavior. Two forces are found during the course of development: positive and negative forces. The negative force leads the blog development to stability and convergence, while critical event causes the positive force to lead the system to move from the stable state towards disturbance, divergence and disorder. The system undergoes a transition from non-chaos to chaos with the introduction of the MSN emoticons on 2004/12/23.

articleTitle: Analysis on managerial strategy of logistics network based on a heterogenous network formation game
abstract: The realistic organizational connection structure of logistics network displays a complicated situation, and the multidimensional heterogeneity is one of most important causes. In this paper, we develop a definition of network heterogeneity in general social and economic network research according to managerial reality with a sharing coefficient. Then, we analysis the network formative mechanism based on modified version of Bala and Goyal's model. Finally, through an analysis on properties of network game equilibrium, we present some suggestions relative to the policy establishment of macroscopic planning and operation strategy for node enterprises.

articleTitle: Coordination mechanism in service supply chains with wholesale price contracts
abstract: With the emergence of integrated service provider operational modes such as the fourth party logistics (4PL), package financial service experts etc., the operational optimization of service supply chains has attracted great attention. Based on wholesale price contract, this paper constructed a pure service two-echelon structure and analyzed the service supply chain's incentive mechanism and coordination mechanism. The paper argues that in order to optimize the benefits of service supply chains, it calls for the service provider to implement incentive mechanism on service supplier, and the incentive mechanism directly affects the coordination condition in service supply chain as well as the flexibility of profit distribution. The results show that service supply chains based on wholesale price contract can realize coordination; And different from the product supply chain, the service supply chain coordination is subject to related parameters from the certain service supply chains such as suppliers' effort cost, demand distribution under different efforts, etc.

articleTitle: Incentive mechanism of 3PL/4PL company based on logistics demander and pure 3PL company
abstract: The third party logistics company develops to the fourth party logistics company is a tendency, and incentive mechanism plays a vital role in the cooperation of 4PL company and 3PL company. The logistics demander, 3PL company and 4PL company are taken into consideration to analyze the optimal incentive level of 4PL company selects in this paper, and our conclusions present that it depends on the ratio of product of weight of the logistics activities and its factor coefficient and the optimal incentive level has a positive correlation with the weight of volume of logistics activities done by 3PL company.

articleTitle: A research of influencing factors of air transport industry competition ability based on product characteristics
abstract: Strengthening the competition ability is an urgent mission for China's air transport industry to survive in the market. In order to find the way of improving the industry competition ability, influencing factors of air transport industry competition ability were analyzed. The connotation of air transport product was defined, and its characteristics and competitive performance level were dissected, by which an analysis model of the influencing factors was built. Then, the specific factors and interactions between them were researched.

articleTitle: A dyadic study of customer and employee personality on service employee affective delivery
abstract: This study explores customer personality (emotional stability) and employee personality (agreeableness) as well as their interaction effect on service employee affective delivery. Data was sampled in two chain restaurants from 259 dyads customers, service employees and supervisors. Results showed that employees' agreeableness increases their affective delivery; and employees' agreeableness enhances the relationship between customers' emotional stability and employees' affective delivery. Implications for personnel selection, placement, and development are derived.

articleTitle: Innovation strategy and firm performance: The moderating role of environmental munificence
abstract: This study examines the relationship between innovation strategy and performance.
